chapter: Chicago, the Woodside, the army and 52nd Street
title: Midwest musicians: Budd Johnson, Jesse Price, Jesse Stone
summary: Collins notes the Midwest produced strong swing reed men and drummers, including Lester Young, Buster Smith, Dick Wilson and Jesse Price.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: He was quite a guy. But Budd Johnson worked with us occasionally too with Roy's band. Budd Johnson and Zutty and it was just a pleasure working with Budd also because Budd was such a tremendous saxophone player, as I told you before. And all of these guys came from Oklahoma or Texas or somewhere, I don't know. The midwest just had
good musicians, very good swing musicians. And -- because let's see -- pardon?
I don't know, you just can't -- it's just hard to explain. But --
But there was Lester Young -- pardon?
Was there any kind of regional music that they grew out of?

I just can't -- I don't know what to attribute it to, you know, just a feeling that was just there, you know. And Chicago kind of had its own thing too. But out of this midwest you had Lester, Budd, Buster Smith, Dick Wilson. These are all tremendous reed men. And they had some very good swing drummers, just pure swing. It was just a pleasure. One of the gentlemen came from Kansas City and played with us awhile, by the name of Jesse Price. Ok sure. (Inaudible).

Yeah, well Jesse was quite a drummer, in his time, and he worked with us, with Roy, in the Three Deuces for awhile. Very good drummer. We used to call him Bopbop. But the midwest had its own thing, you know, so they would come from Kansas City to Chicago and from there, and Jesse Stone also. I don't know whether I mentioned Jesse Stone. He was a tremendous arranger and he had some very
good bands. I think this is a little before your time though.
Thank you, yes, I think so, (Inaudible)

But he had all of the good musicians, you know, Chicago had -- let's see, when he was in Chicago we had Willie Randall, Bud Johnson, of course, and I think Syd Catlett played with him for awhile, also. But just all the best musicians. And I left Chicago with Roy and toured for awhile, and I think my next trip was to Detroit. And we picked up a couple of musicians there, Gerald Wilson, and another -- a saxophone player by the name of Billie Bowen.
